A.explanation: Direction from + flat plate to - curved plate is correct, but straight parallel lines cannot meet the curved lower plate at right angles everywhere.

B.explanation: Arrows point from - to +, which is opposite to the rule that field lines leave positive charge and enter negative charge.

C.explanation: Arrows go from + to - and the lines curve outward so they strike both the flat top plate and the curved bottom plate at 90 degrees.

D.explanation: Lines curve to meet the plates normally, but arrows point upward from - to +, which reverses the correct field direction.

hints: Notice the top flat plate is marked + and the bottom curved plate is marked -, so decide which way a positive test charge would be pushed.
Recall field lines must leave the + plate and enter the - plate, and must meet any conducting surface at right angles.
Compare straight parallel lines with lines that fan out at the edges to see which set can stay perpendicular to the curved lower plate.
walkthrough: Identify the charges: the upper flat horizontal plate is + and the lower upward-curving plate is -.
State the direction rule: electric field direction is the force on a positive test charge, so lines start on + and end on -, meaning downward here from top to bottom.
State the shape rule: field lines meet a conductor surface at 90 degrees. They are perpendicular to the flat top plate, so vertical at the top.
Apply the shape rule to the bottom plate: because it curves upward at the edges, a vertical line would hit it obliquely, so the outer lines must bend outward to still hit it normally.
Check the options: only the diagram with downward arrows and outward-curving outer lines satisfies both direction and right-angle meeting. This is option C.
